metadata.note: The Wheeling & Lake Erie's passenger lines in Ohio and into Wheeling, W.Va., 1880-1938, and the Cleveland Division's predecessor (Connotton Valley / Cleveland & Canton / Cleveland, Canton & Southern) before the W&LE bought it on 5 Aug 1899. Each feature is drawn only for its research report's drawable span. The system's last passenger train ran Cleveland - Wheeling and return on 17 Jul 1938; all intrastate Ohio service was ordered off from 1 Jun 1932.
metadata.ownership_split: Cleveland Division (Cleveland - Canton - Harmon - Coshocton - Zanesville, Chagrin Falls, Canton - Carrollton - Sherrodsville, Minerva): split at 5 Aug 1899 into ccs-* features (Cleveland, Canton and Southern, standing for the Connotton Valley 1880-1885, Cleveland & Canton 1885-1892 and CC&S 1892-1899, successive reorganisations of one property) and wle-* features sharing identical geometry. Canton - Marks is the separate Canton & Waynesburg. NOT splits: Gould acquisition 1880; Pittsburgh-Toledo Syndicate / Wabash stock control 1901-1908 and the 1904 transfer of W&LE stock to the Wabash Pittsburgh Terminal (W&LE kept running its own trains, including the 1904-08 Toledo - Pittsburgh through trains); receiverships 1897-1899 and 1908-1916; reorganisations 1899 and 1916; USRA 1918-1920; Van Sweringen/NKP stock interest; the 1 Dec 1949 NKP lease (eleven years after the last passenger train).
metadata.omitted: Not drawn, per the report's drawable fields: Adena Branch, Adena - St. Clairsville - Neffs (undated station list only, no confirmable passenger year); Lorain & West Virginia, Wellington - Lorain (no passenger evidence, freight only); W&LE trackage rights Wellington - Cleveland over the Big Four from 1913 (freight); Bellaire and Cadiz (town) reaches in the 1952 freight tables; Carrollton & Oneida (pre-W&LE, mule-worked 1859-1866 and unsourced for passengers after). The Pittsburgh through service (Toledo - Pittsburg Junction, 1904-1908 and the 1931 motor train) adds no geometry beyond the W&LE lines drawn here; the Wabash Pittsburgh Terminal / P&WV beyond Pittsburg Junction is a separate road. The Huron - Norwalk original W&LE of 1877-1879 (passengers unproven) and the Ohio & Toledo era on Carrollton - Minerva (1874-c.1879) are not drawn. Canton – Marks (report block 21, Canton & Waynesburg, 1887 anchor): dropped before the PR — no source in hand locates Marks, so the drawn grade was an unsourced identification; omitted rather than risk drawing the wrong line.
metadata.freight_only_check: Every feature ends with its passenger service: the whole W&LE was freight-only after 17 Jul 1938, and every line off the Cleveland - Canton - Harmon - Bowerston - Martins Ferry - Wheeling path lost its trains by 1 Jun 1932 (PUCO order). Carrollton - Sherrodsville is not drawn to its 1936 abandonment. The Feb 1952 Guide's 'FREIGHT SERVICE ONLY' tables are cited but date nothing.
metadata.horsecar_check: Carrollton & Oneida, Carrollton - Oneida, was mule-worked 1859 - 26 Feb 1866 (Wikipedia); it is not drawn at all. No other animal traction on this road.

segments.note: The W&LE's original main line west of the Ohio River: Huron/Norwalk - Massillon opened 9 Jan 1882 (Wikipedia; american-rails has it finished by Nov 1881) and Toledo was reached in Aug 1882 after the 1,311-ft Maumee bridge (american-rails). Through Toledo - Wheeling trains; Wabash through cars Toledo - Pittsburgh ran over it Jul 1904 - May 1908 as W&LE-operated trains. Toledo terminal: Cherry Street, 'one of three passenger stations located on Cherry Street south of Bancroft', removed 1941; Union Depot in the 1905 and 1909 Guides (Fowler). Fowler letters: z = 1896 Guide, b = 1927 company timetable at Kingsway, Fremont, Clyde, Bellevue, Monroeville, Norwalk, Hartland, Clarksfield, Wellington, Spencer, Lodi, Creston, Smithville. A W&LE 'motor train between Pittsburgh and Toledo' was running in Mar 1931 (Butler County Press) - the latest positive evidence, so 1931 is drawn. Passenger service ended no later than 1 Jun 1932, when the Ohio PUCO order authorising abandonment of all the W&LE's intrastate Ohio passenger service took effect (UP wire, Evening Star 5 May 1932: twelve trains discontinued, two kept - the interstate Cleveland - Wheeling pair). The end is therefore bracketed 1931 - Jun 1932 and is NOT an [OPEN] end. CONFLICT: a Lodi depot history says passenger service there ended 17 Jul 1938; treated as that page repeating the system-wide date, recorded not relied on. The Feb 1952 Guide prints Toledo - Fremont as freight only. Gould control from 1880, Wabash/Pittsburgh-Toledo Syndicate stock control 1901-1908, receiverships 1897-99 and 1908-16, USRA 1918-20 and the 1949 NKP lease are not operator changes for drawing purposes. Headway is an ESTIMATE: no per-line train count is sourced before 1932.
sources: Segment-level: start from american-rails (Toledo Aug 1882) and Wikipedia (Huron - Massillon 9 Jan 1882); service confirmed 1896 and 1927 by Fowler's timetable letters and Mar 1931 by the Butler County Press; end bounded by the PUCO order effective 1 Jun 1932 (Evening Star). Headway not sourced.
